facts.statement: The genus Piratosaurus is classified within the group Plesiosauria.
The genus Piratosaurus was named and described by Joseph Leidy in 1865.
facts.quote: named and described by Joseph Leidy in 1865

facts.statement: The only known fossil evidence for Piratosaurus is a single tooth designated as holotype USNM V 1000.
facts.quote: It is known only from the holotype, USNM V 1000, a tooth

facts.statement: Fossils of Piratosaurus date to the Late Cretaceous period.
The type species was discovered in Late Cretaceous-aged rocks in the Red River basin of Manitoba.
facts.quote: discovered in Late Cretaceous-aged rocks in the Red River basin of Manitoba

facts.statement: Piratosaurus is considered a dubious genus of plesiosaur that may belong to the family Polycotylidae.
facts.quote: Piratosaurus (meaning "pirate lizard") is a dubious genus of plesiosaur possibly belonging to the Polycotylidae

facts.statement: Some researchers have incorrectly assumed the fossils were found in Minnesota.
facts.quote: at least one researcher erroneously assumed it was found in Minnesota
